_schema.logs: one entry per log (a log = 1–2 weeks on one question, NOT one per small step); date = start YYYY-MM-DD (matches folder); optional updated = last change; status ∈ running|done|closed|blocked|failed; path relative to experiments/
_schema.format: optional per entry: "deck" | "log" (default log). Deck = the meeting slide-deck record (README.md "Deck"), folder <project>/decks/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/; same scope rule (one deck = one question, update the open one). Existing entries without the key are logs.
_schema.note: Index pages render from this file, sorted by updated||date. Agents: prefer UPDATING the project's open log (bump updated, refresh tldr/status) over appending a new entry — see README.md 'Scope'.

3d-wam.title: 3D-WAM
3d-wam.tagline: Observation and action as one dense labeled 3D point set; a single generative model predicts total scene flow (human + Sharpa training); claim: robot-zero-shot execution of tasks demonstrated only by humans. Concept stage.
3d-wam.now: Motion history conditioning (C1) is the first arm to beat a zero-flow predictor — ADE 13.82 vs 14.66, object direction cosine 2.9x. Duration and five architectural interventions did not. C2 (history + duration) running.

dpp-bmw.title: BMW & Frontier Demo
dpp-bmw.tagline: Dexterous Point Policy on real human demonstrations, two tasks in one place. BMW assembly rig (4-view: MANO hand pose + VGGT-Omega object points + HaWoR contact) and Frontier Demo logistics (ego-stereo HMD: promptable segmentation + VGGT-Omega stereo depth). No sim, no residual RL.

now.text: BMW: 7 base policies trained & verified @100k (left-hand corrected); eval/rollout next. Frontier Demo (logistics): rig confirmed ego-stereo only across v1-v6 — no external view; mask-free object points proven on one episode, hand pose from ego-stereo not yet built.

dex-pointwam.tagline: Dexterous-hand point-cloud world-action model (EgoDex-pretrained) — sim + real deployment.

dex-point-policy.title: Dexterous Point Policy
dex-point-policy.tagline: Point-cloud dexterous manipulation policy — ICLR 2027 resubmission workstream.

now.text: Functional-retargeter restructure: design CLOSED v1.0 (DESIGN.md) - task-agnostic R, MANO-theta both ways, two-hand play pairing. Next: critical-path checks C1-C4 (MANO-in-Isaac, DexCanvas, EgoDex theta, g_E rebase), then the Inspire pilot pending sign-off.

logs.title: Faster, then bigger — the p-series: throughput, batch geometry, a 320M expert (deck #9)
logs.tldr: Deck #9: training was already bf16 — but the A100 runs at ~9% MFU on micro-batch 16; p1 recovers 2–2.5× (batch 32×1, torch.compile, fused optimizer). Accumulation adds no speed on one GPU — effective 64 is the ceiling at 320M. p4 scales the video-DiT to π0.5 action-expert dims (d1024×18L ≈ 320M), 5 epochs of the no-hot3d basis ≈ 11–14 h on the h100 partition. 120M stays the screening model; i0/i5 land 110k overnight.

logs.title: Dataset usage guide — EgoDex and VITRA human data
logs.tldr: Consumer-facing usage guide as a meeting deck, deliberately minimal: where the data lives and which keys to read. Two artifact families over the same episodes, joined by filename — maskcap sidecars for the 3D encoder, flow H5s for PointWAM, all under /virtual_lab/sjw_alinlab/beomjun/ with manifests/a7_stems.txt and manifests/generation_index.tsv as the caption-subset selectors. Keys: camera_0_scene_flows (11,N,3) world metres, camera_0_scene_colors, embodiment_joints (ARKit GT on EgoDex, reconstructed MANO on VITRA; 12-kp dex view = indices [0,24,5,15,20,10] x 2 hands), camera_0_robot_valid as the idle-hand mask; on the sidecar side camera_0_instance_id, global_siglip2 (G,1152) as the encoder target, global_captions and global_is_agent. Sample visualisations for both families. Per-part statistics, complete schemas and the load snippet stay in the 2026-08-27 log.

logs.title: Every number we had was one dataset
logs.tldr: The val loader gates every sampler on split=='train', so it walks the chunk index in file order and the first 400 batches are 100% arctic: every evaluation number this project has reported came from 32-48 chunks of one dataset. Restated on a stratified six-dataset val (validated to reproduce the old probe digit-for-digit on the old 48 chunks), the ranking survives but absolute values roughly halve and nothing beats a zero predictor; D6 at 110k steps lands below a 3.4k-step arm with history on. A paired bootstrap says only three of nine single-flag ablations were ever distinguishable from their control. Eight new arms: interface tokens null, spatial RoPE negative (-0.008 at 10k) despite looking like a steady +0.015 on the arctic curve, uniform k=4 negative (-0.007, settling the patchify question). The one real gain is data composition: dropping hot3d beats its own data-volume control by +0.008 [+0.002,+0.014]. And a model trained only on human hands keeps 79% of its hand direction accuracy on the Sharpa hand zero-shot, gap -0.052 [-0.091,-0.015] over 258 matched pairs.

logs.title: Multi-stream joint attention did not fix it — a falsified prediction
logs.tldr: MMDiT/MSAT-style per-entity-class MLP parameters with joint attention, parameters matched at 119.94 M, three cells at 2,200 steps. The prediction that objects far from hands would stop moving is falsified: they move 0.56-2.64 cm against 0.06 cm true, and object motion overshoots ground truth (52-156%). Hand motion unchanged. The motion-weighted loss remains the only lever on magnitude and is what drives the overshoot.

logs.title: Collapse defeated, direction missing — motion-weighted loss and an autoregressive head
logs.tldr: A motion-weighted loss raises generated motion from 12% to 73% of ground truth (hand 17%->48%), monotone in both runs, so mean-collapse is beaten. Accuracy does not follow: no checkpoint beats both the zero-flow and velocity-extrapolation baselines. The autoregressive head gives the best trade (ADE 0.078 at 50% motion) and drifts on long sequences. Next: drift control, contact-gated object motion, a direction-only metric.

logs.title: Why it does not work yet — the pilot predicts no motion, and why
logs.tldr: The 12-h pilot trains cleanly but does not beat a zero-flow baseline (best-of-8 0.0312 vs 0.0319 m; sampled motion 8x too small). Oracle-velocity and foreign-target tests exclude sampler bugs, leakage, capacity and normalisation: the velocity target lets the model denoise instead of using the scene, so sampling collapses to the conditional mean. Fix: predict the flow, add a regression baseline, rescale the auxiliaries.

logs.title: Architecture & training — design C, pilot chain launched (deck #2)
logs.tldr: Design C trained (12k steps, conditioning levers). Honest verdict: the model does not beat a zero-flow baseline (best-of-8 0.0312 vs 0.0319 m; wins 38 % of chunks) and sampling noise (36 mm) dwarfs conditioning effects (1–9 mm), so the transfer probes are uninformative until the conditional is learned.

logs.title: Datasets & train data structure — six human sources + CHORD Sharpa, 15 Hz · N = 2048 (deck #1)
logs.tldr: Deck #1: six human datasets (5,319 episodes, 19.6 h) + CHORD Sharpa TACO release (1,215); preprocessed at 15 Hz, N = 2048 → 4,022 human + 1,148 Sharpa episodes; units consistent (metres); sample = metric points · group label · 48-d flow · masks · contact · T5 text.

logs.title: A human→Inspire retargeter trained on 4-view high-quality assembly data
logs.tldr: R and R⁻¹ trained on bmw_0821 (60 runs, 33,191 frames, 4-view high-precision hand pose). Position-mode retargeting maps the grasp-region aperture (0–5 cm) nearly 1:1 (human 0/2.7/5.0 → robot 2.1/2.6/4.9 cm; corr 0.664), saturating only at the physically-unreachable open extreme. R⁻¹ reconstructs the full 21-keypoint hand from 5 robot fingertips at 7.7 mm all-joint / 6.1 mm intermediate held-out MAE. Different task from the openarm-sim work; targets Inspire hardware. Sim rollout pending an environment.

logs.title: Retargeter & teleop-mix debugging in openarm-sim — seven bugs fixed, still 0/24
logs.tldr: Debugging the openarm-sim deployment of the 21kp policy + dexret Inspire retargeter, organized by the rollout clips. Seven implementation bugs found and fixed, each verified by measurement: obs R⁻¹ OOD + Kabsch contamination (stalling), dexret vector→position (finger opening), scale 1.15 miscalibration, arm-IK/finger scale mismatch, teleop object-cloud 6cm hand-removal (object deleted during grasp, 28.8→0.8cm), proprio zero-fill, wrist orientation. Every condition still SR 0/24 — the bottleneck is the policy's alignment/approach and a teleop→sim domain gap, not the retargeter.

logs.title: bmw_0821: 60-run batch to 7 verified base policies — initdest/subtask matrix + point-shift augmentation
logs.tldr: New 60-run BMW batch taken from raw 4-camera rosbags to trainable data (4-view MANO hand pose, single-view HaWoR contact, VGGT-Omega object points, all in the BA world frame) and two rounds of base-policy training. Exp1: initdest/subtask matrix (3 policies). Exp2: subsample (2x/1x) x point-augmentation (none/1cm/5cm), all subtask, no initdest (4 policies). All 7 reach 100k and torch-load clean. Point-shift augmentation (one spherical shift per sample applied to hand+object+action+ego) verified consistent: relative hand-object geometry preserved to +/-1cm even at a 50cm shift. Object order jig,ecu,bracket,drill confirmed against masks. Eval/rollout is next.

logs.title: One frozen human policy, N functional retargeters — verified 4/5, design closed v1.0
logs.tldr: Workstream restructured around a frozen human-data base policy + a learned per-embodiment retargeter whose objective is FUNCTIONAL: the object must follow the source's 3D trajectory. Theory verdict 4/5; 4 papers read in full + a 26-work sweep (no 5/5 collision - the paper hangs on one ablation: the same retargeter trained on kinematic vs object-motion-matched pairs). Design closed same-day at v1.0 after five discussion rounds: MANO-theta interfaces both ways (R: theta->q residual over a geometric prior; R-1: q->theta), W=1 per-step at control rate, wrist 6D + arm IK outside R, and a hard principle - the retargeter is TASK-AGNOSTIC (no robot demos, no task data; pairs from two-hand sim play where the MANO hand leads and the robot tracks the recorded object trajectory on the same clock; benchmark objects held out). Spec: DPP-ICLR2027/retargeter/DESIGN.md. Pilot ~3-4 H100-d gated on C1-C4 checks + sign-off.

logs.title: Scene density: the 12k budget, EE-centered sampling, and a VGGT-Omega proposal
logs.tldr: The near-field starvation is an ALLOCATION problem, not a sensor problem: 54% of the 12,000-point budget lands beyond 1.5 m and ~2% within 20 cm of the hand, while the source holds 5x more near-hand geometry than the random cap keeps. EE-centered sampling (banded/gaussian) recovers 3-5x near-hand density at equal budget, on both sim and EgoDex sides. Every scheme is still a heuristic for spending a capped token budget PTv3 imposes by construction - a VGGT-Omega encoder proposal (pixel-dense geometry, ~1,041 tokens/frame, perspective foveation for free) is filed with two 1-GPU-hour de-riskers pending.

logs.title: Initial development and pretraining on EgoDex
logs.tldr: Porting PointWAM to a 12-keypoint dexterous hand and pretraining on EgoDex. At 5.2M clips held-out robot_l2_moved is 0.06057 +/- 0.00017 m; the world-modelling branch buys -4.7% (z~12) and the gap GROWS with scale rather than washing out. Open-loop only, and the run was still improving at the budget limit.

logs.title: Closed-loop evaluation on the DPP task
logs.tldr: The same checkpoint picks nothing up. Not a stall and not oscillation: a COHERENT trajectory (chunk-to-chunk cosine +0.99) converging on a fixed point 16 cm from the object. Three of our own statistics retracted. Leading candidate is a chunk-length mismatch: our shipped chunk spans 30 raw frames against DPP's 16, so three finetune arms (16, 16 at half resolution, 30 frames) are in flight. Corrected 2026-08-03: the SOURCE RATE IS NOT SETTLED - the 20 Hz figure is a delivered-rate label, not a sensor measurement, so the arms are defined in frames and no result depends on it.

logs.title: Four poses cannot estimate a success rate
logs.tldr: The openarm-sim eval driver placed the object at the exact centre of its grid cell every episode, so a 512-episode run was four initial conditions repeated 128 times. Fixing it (1cm per-episode jitter) moves the 3-object mean only 23.2 -> 22.9% but changes what every number means: cells had saturated at 0/128 and 128/128, and the tennis ball scored 1.4% at the centre pose vs 6.4% under jitter, a 4.6x per-object error. Cross-hand re-run at 96 eps/hand now has non-overlapping intervals (Inspire 25.0% [17.4-34.5] vs Wuji/Sharpa 0/96 [0-3.85]) with IK residuals reproducing the earlier study to within a millimetre. And the contact-label question finally resolved, paired on identical initial conditions at a matched 370k steps: the HUMAN label wins bottle (-8.0, p=0.031) and box (-10.9, p=5e-05) and loses only ball (+2.5, where neither policy is competent) - the opposite of the 07-30 reading, which had compared checkpoints at different steps selected on bottle alone. Since that human label is one grasp bit copied across five fingers, a 1-bit label trains a better policy than a genuine 5-bit one.

logs.title: Rebuilding the object points beats the shipped pipeline; the contact-label winner flips by object
logs.tldr: Rebuilt DPP's object points (128 -> 2048 pts, mask erosion -> depth-gradient rejection, sensor-metric depth fusion) and trained two otherwise-identical finetunes that differ only in the contact label. Mean success_at_end over bottle/box/ball at 512 episodes each: learned-tactile label 36.8%, human label 31.7%, shipped 128-pt baseline 23.2%. The two labels trade places by object (human wins bottle 76.6 vs 49.0, loses box 14.6 vs 44.7 and ball 3.9 vs 16.6), and both checkpoints were selected on bottle alone, so no label claim survives. Measured why the labels differ at all: the human annotation is one grasp bit copied across five fingers (1.21 distinct finger columns of 5 over 69k frames, contact head 0.98 acc) while the learned tactile is a real 5-bit target (0.70). Also found the benchmark has four initial conditions, not 512 - the driver runs with zero position jitter. [2026-07-31] Protocol note: these numbers are from the 4-condition benchmark. Re-measured under 1cm jitter the 3-object mean holds (23.2 -> 22.9%) but the ball goes 1.4 -> 6.4%; the label comparison is being re-run at matched budget with a pre-registered paired analysis.

logs.title: Contact generalizes to PnP/Tool; the 6-point abstraction breaks on hand scale
logs.tldr: Learned tactile-contact transfers to PnP (F1 0.70) and Tool (spray power-grip recovers ring+pinky; microwave's low F1 is a thumb-free GT artifact). DPP in the openarm-sim PnP benchmark scores 29.2% with Inspire (reproducing the ~27% baseline bit-for-bit) and 0/24 with both Wuji (20-DOF) and Sharpa (22-DOF) — the cause is finger reach, not DOF count: the retargeting IK displaces the wrist 2.8-5.4 cm. Rescaling fingertip targets fixes the IK and still scores 0/24, because DPP's input is six points too. Two earlier sim claims withdrawn; the debugging also found the bottle's object cloud smears past 30 cm on 14.2% of fine-tune frames (missing depth-gradient filter). [2026-07-31] Re-run at 96 eps/hand on the jittered protocol: reproduces with non-overlapping intervals (Inspire 25.0% [17.4-34.5] vs 0/96 [0-3.85]).

logs.title: SpaceFormer's caption protocol transfers to ego video; its static clustering does not
logs.tldr: Human-data engine for the PointWAM 3D encoder: SAM2 masks + VLM captions + SigLIP2 targets from EgoDex/VITRA ego video. A faithful SpaCeFormer-3M re-implementation (A.6/A.7 prompts verbatim, MaskClustering params, Gemma-3, 5 captions/instance) run head-to-head on 10 episodes: captions are adopted-worthy (earlier Gemma failure was protocol mismatch), but static MaskClustering collapses on ego motion — coverage 94.3%→57.9%, instances 12→6.2/ep — quantitatively justifying our scene-flow merge. Recommended default: hybrid. EgoDex campaign ~178k/324k (55%); two-pass fleet (SAM2 pass + Gemma pass) with A/B-validated fast masker; 15 new-dataset demos (DexYCB/AEA/EPIC).

logs.title: Human data, ready to consume — paths, statistics, schemas
logs.tldr: Usage guide for the two consumers, with a live status board. PointWAM is unblocked: the full flow corpus (324,167 EgoDex + 825,935 VITRA) is complete and validated. 3D encoder: EgoDex coverage closed at 100%; the remaining work is homogeneity (A.7 193,492 / v3 97,162 / pre-fix v0-v2 33,513), done 09-01. VITRA sidecars now run at a measured 801 episodes/h/GPU after caching the episode enumeration that was costing every job 57 minutes of NFS scanning — VITRA completes 09-02.

logs.title: Rebuilt as a video generation model — 10 Hz data, time as a token axis, three designs (deck #6)
logs.tldr: Deck #6: the pilot rebuilt to the video-generation contract. Data re-preprocessed at 10 Hz, human only, chunk stride 1, 512 points per entity (5,645 episodes, 848,622 chunks). Time becomes a token axis instead of 48 channels; tokens are Hilbert-serialized patches of 8 points (PTv3 construction used as Wan's patch embed, unpatchify verified exact); RoPE on the frame index. The loss is stripped to plain masked MSE — no rigidity, no contact, no motion reweighting, no adaptive batch-RMS normalisation, no autoregressive arm. Three parameter-matched arms at ~120 M: D1 patches + full attention, D2 one token per point-frame + PTv3 windowed attention, D3 = D1 + block-causal temporal attention, taken from MolmoMotion's finding that its autoregressive head beats its own flow-matching head because each step conditions on what came before (verified exactly: perturbing later frames changes frame 0's output by 0.0). RESULTS: no arm beats the zero-flow baseline (14.66 cm); all four slide along a single ADE-vs-motion trade-off curve toward the zero predictor, and D3 (causal time) is the only one holding its motion at 63 %. Error decomposition says direction, not magnitude, is the wall — cosine(pred, gt) 0.145, perfect magnitude buys 8 % and still loses, perfect direction buys 36 % and wins; cosine is worst at t=1 and rises with the horizon, so a shorter horizon or a closed loop would be worse. Two of our own hypotheses died: the '852 % object overshoot' was a mean-of-ratios artefact (true 111 %), and per-step normalisation deepened collapse rather than fixing it. A fourth arm finetuning MolmoMotion-4B is blocked on imagery that does not exist in our data, but zero-shot its hand flow beats the zero baseline on 5 of 9 episodes with no hand data in pretraining.

logs.title: Overnight — the model was better than we could measure (deck #7)
logs.tldr: Deck #7: ten trained arms, ten ablation arms and nine measurement-only investigations. Both long runs finished at 110k steps fully annealed: history + duration reaches cosine 0.457 and ADE 12.89, duration alone 0.282 and 16.69 — losing to a zero predictor by 23 %, so history is worth more than nine times the compute. The decisive finding is a metric one: best-of-8 sampling reaches cosine 0.837 against a model-free ceiling of 0.861, so the distribution already contains near-optimal trajectories and the failure is SELECTION. A 36-recipe inference sweep on an existing checkpoint reaches ADE 10.41, 29 % better than predicting nothing, with no training at all. A new interaction-quality suite adapted from the hand-object generation literature (CG-HOI, Text2HOI, HO-Flow, JointHOI) shows object shape improving 4.8x and contact placement 2x across arms, while objects still deform 23x beyond physics and contact IoU sits at 38.8 %. In the ablation x1 parameterisation halves penetration and improves shape 33-36 %; the rigidity loss made shape worse, not better.
